meta.scope: Present-day religion and language distribution, Sudan and South Sudan.
meta.rules: Shares only where a cited page states them (all APPROXIMATE). Religion shares are Pew estimates as reported by the US State Dept 2023 IRF reports (government source, labelled). Languages: Glottolog country lists only; no speaker shares or scripts are given because no opened source stated them. Region is country level unless the cited text names sub-national areas. place_ids only from db/cities.json, no coordinates. Unregistered sources: see /workspace/audit/people_religion_sources_to_register.md.
meta.gaps: No UNHCR/OCHA/UNFPA/UN Statistics or Ethnologue page with religion/language figures was opened this pass; not cited.

religions.share_basis: Pew 2020 estimate as reported by US State Dept

citation.source_type: government (U.S. Department of State), citing Pew data
citation.quote: The Pew Research Center’s 2020 data estimated that 91 percent of the population was Muslim, 5.4 percent Christian, 2.8 percent followed indigenous religions, and the remainder followed other religions or were unaffiliated.

citation_extra.source_type: government (U.S. Department of State), citing Pew data
citation_extra.quote: Almost all Muslims in the country identify as Sunni, although there are significant distinctions among followers of different Sunni traditions, particularly among Sufi orders.

religions.region: Sudan (national); concentrated in major cities, parts of the Nuba Mountains (South Kordofan) and Blue Nile
religions.share_basis: Pew 2020 estimate as reported by US State Dept; religious advocacy groups estimate non-Muslims at more than 13 percent

citation.source_type: government (U.S. Department of State), citing Pew data
citation.quote: The Pew Research Center’s 2020 data estimated that 91 percent of the population was Muslim, 5.4 percent Christian, 2.8 percent followed indigenous religions, and the remainder followed other religions or were unaffiliated.

citation_extra.source_type: government (U.S. Department of State), citing Pew data
citation_extra.quote: Christians are resident throughout the country, primarily in major cities such as Khartoum, Port Sudan, Kassala, Gedaref, El Obeid, and El Fasher. Christians also are concentrated in some parts of the Nuba Mountains, South Kordofan State, and in parts of Blue Nile State.

citation_extra.source_type: government (U.S. Department of State), citing Pew data
citation_extra.quote: Some religious advocacy groups estimate non-Muslims constitute more than 13 percent of the population.

religions.region: Sudan; primarily Blue Nile and South Kordofan States
religions.share_basis: Pew 2020 estimate 2.8%; government statistics: less than 1 percent (sources disagree)

citation.source_type: government (U.S. Department of State), citing Pew data
citation.quote: The Pew Research Center’s 2020 data estimated that 91 percent of the population was Muslim, 5.4 percent Christian, 2.8 percent followed indigenous religions, and the remainder followed other religions or were unaffiliated.

citation_extra.source_type: government (U.S. Department of State), citing Pew data
citation_extra.quote: Government statistics indicate less than 1 percent of the population, primarily in Blue Nile and South Kordofan States, adhere to traditional African religious beliefs.

religions.share_basis: Pew-Templeton 2020 estimate as reported by US State Dept; displacement and pastoral migration make estimates difficult

citation.source_type: government (U.S. Department of State), citing Pew data
citation.quote: The 2020 Pew-Templeton Global Religious Futures Project report estimated Christians make up 60.5 percent of the population; followers of Indigenous (animist) religions, 32.9 percent; and Muslims, 6.2 percent.

citation_extra.source_type: government (U.S. Department of State), citing Pew data
citation_extra.quote: make it difficult to accurately estimate the overall population and its religious demography.
